QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_20

question.text: Mr. Anand, an Indian citizen leaving India as a crew member of an Indian ship, was present in India for 100 days during PY 2024-25. His total stay in India during the 4 preceding years was 400 days. What is his residential status?

answer.text: Non-Resident, since he was present less than 182 days
Non-Resident, since the crew clause requires 182 days in the current year plus 365 days in the preceding 4 years and he fails the 182-day test
Resident, since he satisfies the 60-day + 365-day test
Resident, since the 120-day relaxation applies to Indian citizens

explanation.text: The Logic: For an Indian citizen leaving India as a crew member of an Indian ship, residency requires 182 days in the current year together with 365 days in the 4 preceding previous years. The relaxed 60-day basic-condition test does not apply to this category. Mr. Anand was present for only 100 days in the current year, which is less than 182, so he fails the crew clause and is a Non-Resident — regardless of the 400 days in the preceding 4 years. The Trap: Candidates may apply the general 60+365 test or the 120-day rule for Indian citizens, forgetting that crew members of Indian ships have a dedicated test that requires 182 days in the current year. Note: The 182-day current-year leg is the controlling threshold for the crew clause; failing it ends the analysis at Non-Resident.
